text:
Recent research supports separating observed behavior, stated preference and evidence sufficiency. [ReCRec (2024)](https://zlstwebsite.github.io/Zlst/publication/recrec-reasoning-the-causes-of-implicit-feedback-for-debiased-recommendation/) distinguishes noninteraction caused by nonexposure from dislike; [RecSys 2025 research](https://arxiv.org/abs/2508.05398) shows that exposure and candidate sampling affect evaluation reliability. For this audit, record items shown, feedback received and assessable judgments separately. Report reason-specific rejection counts divided by explicitly assessed exposures, alongside response and abstention rates; unanswered items must not become rejections. Twenty users support exploratory diagnosis, with per-category counts and uncertainty, rather than population-wide purchase-intent claims.

A practical rubric—an application of these findings, not an established benchmark—should separately capture choose-now intent, unnecessary duplication, explicit incompatibility and unidentified content, with an unknown option for every dimension. Require supporting history/title/description evidence or explicit user feedback for each judgment. Lexical similarity can nominate review cases but cannot establish ownership, fulfilled demand or incompatibility. Missing compatibility information remains unknown. [Abstain-QA (2025)](https://aclanthology.org/2025.coling-main.627/) evaluates both answerable and unanswerable cases, supporting checks for unsupported assertions and unnecessary abstention rather than rewarding abstention frequency alone.

[ConSiDERS (2024)](https://aclanthology.org/2024.acl-long.63/) recommends clear guidelines, independent pilot annotation and iterative clarification of ambiguous examples. Double-code a shared subset; report raw agreement, chance-corrected agreement and label-specific disagreements before adjudication. Agreement concerns consistent application of the rubric to evidence; users’ different preferences are not annotation errors. Keep feedback-derived audit findings separate from the fixed macro validation HR@10 used for model selection.
